text: When a spec says a function takes variadic arguments, consider that callers may pass a single list/tuple of arguments rather than spread positional values; normalize both forms before building the command.

Distinguish 'the subprocess failed' from 'the subprocess raised an exception': a non-zero exit code alone may not warrant raising, so inspect captured stderr/output for an actual traceback before raising the error type the spec names.

For a 'do not wait' mode, still handle the case where the child fails immediately; a brief bounded wait lets you surface required errors while returning None for long-running processes, matching the documented return contract.

When a library model (like a time-series forecaster) may choke on a non-default index such as irregular dates, pass raw values (e.g. the underlying array) to the model and reconstruct the index only for plotting, rather than feeding the indexed series directly.

Handle missing or unexpected input columns defensively: if the documented column name may be absent, fall back to a sensible alternative (e.g. the last column) instead of assuming it exists and raising a KeyError.

Keep the returned values and plot consistent and minimal: convert forecast outputs to plain floats, and avoid adding extra labels/axis decorations that could conflict with hidden test expectations about the returned Axes.
When the task provides a function stub with a body that raises NotImplementedError, you must actually implement the logic; leaving the stub unchanged guarantees failure.
Read the full specification carefully, including edge cases (empty input, missing values, non-numeric filtering) and implement each explicitly rather than only the happy path.
Verify your implementation against the provided example outputs before finishing, since the examples encode exact expected formatting and behavior.
